message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar appears in the **Only Fools and Horses** episode titled **"Yuppy Love"**. This was the first episode of **Series 6**, which originally aired on **January 8, 1989** on BBC1.

In the scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool" and goes to lean seductively on the bar, unaware that the barman has lifted the counter hatch. He falls straight through the gap and onto the floor, while Trigger looks around confused about where Del has gone.

This scene is frequently voted one of the funniest moments in British sitcom history. Interestingly, it was almost quite different - writer John Sullivan originally intended Del to simply stumble and catch himself, based on a real-life incident he'd witnessed. However, David Jason insisted on falling all the way through, drawing on his experience in stage farces. Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally scripted to appear in the scene; Roger Lloyd Pack happened to be at the BBC on the filming day and was written in, with much of the humour coming from his bemused reaction as he circles around looking for Del.
